candidates.dedupeCheck: No seed incident or candidate shares this identity. The 2026-11-11 batch excluded EDR-killer and EDR-evasion landscape reports (Halcyon, ESET, Cyware); this one differs because Sophos describes a specific framework found on an endpoint in a customer tenant.

claims.statement: Sophos says the activity surfaced when an anomalous endpoint in a customer tenant raised alerts for payloads in a test folder under a user's Documents directory, and several files there pointed to a wider framework built to evade detection.

Sophos describes a lab of virtual machines: Windows Server 2022 hosts for testing against the Sophos agent and the CrowdStrike agent, a control host with no EDR, and an Ubuntu host running a Sliver C2 server; Windows Defender is also named as a target.

Sophos says the actor used the Cursor IDE and Claude Opus agents to write, test and revise EDR-bypass tools, with MCP passing code issues and commits to a Git repository, and that some scripts were partly AI-generated.

Sophos assesses that AI mainly coordinated workflows and supported experimentation, while the evasion work was a structured engineering cycle with human review; its automated Active Directory discovery panel chose from predefined actions and is not described as an autonomous LLM.
Agent reports claimed near-universal success against EDR agents after iteration, but Sophos says the documented output does not necessarily support that conclusion.
Sophos researchers link this development activity to known ransomware deployment and data theft operations, and say the red-team framing was likely used to get around model guardrails.

unresolvedQuestions: Owner decision: is this an incident or a source-registry item? Sophos describes one observed endpoint in an unnamed customer tenant (closer to the reviewed Cairn intrusion than to the landscape reports excluded on 2026-11-11), but no victim impact is reported.
Unknown: the Sophos post states no publication date; a ThaiCERT summary seen in search was dated 2026-06-05. Confirm before promotion.

Unknown: whether the actor's tooling ran against the customer's environment beyond the test folder, or whether the endpoint was the actor's own registered device. Sophos describes it only as anomalous.
No actor is named; the ransomware and data-theft link is Sophos's assessment and must not be recorded as attribution.
Disputed: the agents' claimed EDR-bypass success rate is not supported by the documented output, per Sophos. Do not cite it as fact.
Proposed category link after promotion: endpoint-security (related_to). Does not imply that any EDR product, including the ones tested, was or was not bypassed in production.
Dark Reading secondary was not fetched; only the Sophos primary was read.
